newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's FIS lobbies West on torture supplies.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's FIS lobbies West on torture supplies.

text.p: Algeria's outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) urged Western countries on Wednesday to investigate allegations by Amnesty International that their firms supplied torture equipment to Algiers.

"Although Algeria has ratified international accords banning torture, the Algerian military authorities continuously resort to torture detained or imprisoned people by all sorts of means including electric shocks," the FIS said in a statement.
The statement was received in Paris from the FIS leadership in exile, which is based in Germany.
In a report published last week, Amnesty International documented cases of electro-shock torture in 50 countries and said at least 100 companies around the world had marketed such weapons.

"The most worrying and most terrible issue is the implication of dozens of Western companies, as Amnesty International revealed in its last report, in supplying the Algerian military authorities with means for electric torture," the FIS said.
"We therefore ask Western countries concerned to launch investigations on these sales so as to sanction companies and punish those responsible," the FIS said.
It also urged the United Nations to adopt a resolution banning the production of torture equipment.

The FIS was outlawed after 1992 parliamentary elections it was poised to win were scrapped. About 60,000 people have died since then in the strife pitting government forces against Moslem rebels, including the FIS' armed wing Islamic Salvation Army (AIS).
